tests/rm/ignorable.sh.note: rm -f ignores ENOTDIR as well as ENOENT (GNU nonexistent_file_errno). core/rm.xsh nonexistent_errno; native test test_rm_force_ignores_a_file_used_as_a_directory.

tests/rm/inaccessible.sh.note: build-gnu.sh rewrites the expected line from $EACCES to "rm: cannot remove 'rel': No such file or directory". Real GNU expects Permission denied, and XSH prints exactly that (GNU unlink on this kernel returns EACCES). Wording-conflict if the patched line is required.

tests/rm/interactive-once.sh.note: GNU prompts for write-protected files when stdin is a terminal (or ---presume-input-tty) under -I too. core/rm.xsh automatic mode now covers -I. Native test test_rm_interactive_once_prompts_for_write_protected_files_on_a_terminal.

tests/rm/many-dir-entries-vs-OOM.sh.note: Skipped because get_min_ulimit_v_ finds no working limit: XSH du exits 101 under ulimit -v 50000 KB and works at 100000 KB, so the XSH runtime's address-space floor is above the probe ceiling. The test also needs a 200000-entry tree. Needs a smaller runtime footprint (not an owned file).

tests/rmdir/t-slash.sh.note: rmdir -p walks the operand text as GNU remove_parents does: 'dir/' removes only 'dir', never '.'. Parent failures use GNU's 'failed to remove directory' wording. Native tests test_rmdir_parents_walks_the_operand_text_with_trailing_slashes and test_rmdir_parent_failure_uses_gnu_directory_wording.

tests/mkdir/p-3.sh.note: Path.mkdir and other host_path operations (src/runtime/eval.rs host_path) join relative names onto the evaluator's absolute cwd, so mkdir a/b under a cwd whose ancestor lost search permission fails with EACCES. GNU mkdirat succeeds (checked via the oracle). Needs a cwd-relative (*at) mkdir operation from the runtime.

tests/readlink/can-e.sh.note: After the cwd is removed, readlink -e . must fail with status 1. The runtime falls back to "." when current_dir() fails (src/runtime/eval.rs:3426), so fs.cwd() returns "." and the result is "/.". With that block excluded in a scratch copy, the rest of the test passes.

tests/readlink/can-f.sh.note: Same removed-cwd cause as can-e (src/runtime/eval.rs:3426 fallback to "."). Remaining assertions pass in a scratch copy with the removed-cwd block excluded.

tests/readlink/can-m.sh.note: Same removed-cwd cause as can-e (src/runtime/eval.rs:3426 fallback to "."). Remaining assertions pass in a scratch copy with the removed-cwd block excluded.

tests/stat/stat-printf.pl.note: The brief names stat-printf.sh; the file is stat-printf.pl. build-gnu.sh rewrites 'warning: unrecognized escape' to 'warning: incomplete hex escape', so hex-3 expects non-GNU wording. GNU 9.11 and the 9.12 source print "unrecognized escape '\x'" and output x; XSH now does the same. end-bs (backslash at end of format) is fixed. Wording-conflict for hex-3.

tests/stat/stat-fmt.sh.note: QUOTING_STYLE is validated only when a %N or %Qn directive renders; %% is a literal percent (GNU stat initialize_quoting_style). core/stat.xsh quotes_name; native test test_stat_quoting_style_is_checked_only_for_quoting_directives.

tests/touch/obsolescent.sh.note: The obsolete [MMDDhhmm[YY]][.ss] operand applies only when _POSIX2_VERSION < 200112, with a trailing year only in 69-99, and warns unless POSIXLY_CORRECT is set. core/touch.xsh obsolete_stamp; native test test_touch_obsolete_operand_uses_posix_version_and_yearly_range and test_touch_obsolete_operand_warns_without_posixly_correct.

tests/date/date-sec.sh.note: date accepts a bare clock with a zone offset (21:04 +0100) in core/lib/date_parse.xsh. Native test test_date_clock_with_zone_offset_and_signed_day_counts.

tests/test/test-N.sh.note: Setup failed because touch -d '12:00 today -2 days' was rejected. The date_parse fixes accept signed day counts after a day word and a trailing day word after a clock (also used by touch -d). Covered by test_date_clock_with_zone_offset_and_signed_day_counts; test -N itself was already correct.

tests/chmod/setgid.sh.note: A symbolic clause with no class may be a whole octal mode after its operator (=7777,-5022), as in GNU mode_compile; with a class it is invalid. core/chmod.xsh; native test test_chmod_clause_octal_mode_covers_the_whole_mode.

tests/chown/deref.sh.note: A dangling link named under --dereference reports 'cannot dereference' (GNU chown-core); a missing name keeps 'cannot access'. core/lib/perm.xsh change_owner; native test test_chown_dereference_of_dangling_link_names_the_link.

tests/id/uid.sh.note: A leading '+' makes the operand a numeric ID, and id NAME lists groups through idtools.account_ids instead of refusing. core/id.xsh find_user; the now-unused idtools.unsupported_user_groups is removed. Native tests test_id_plus_prefix_is_numeric_and_named_group_lists_work; test_id_named_users updated from the old refusal to GNU output.

tests/id/zero.sh.note: Same change as tests/id/uid.sh: group lists for named users (id -G, -Gz and the -u/-g variants) now come from the account database.

tests/nice/nice.sh.note: If the privilege warning cannot be written, nice exits 125 without running the command (GNU nice.c ferror path). core/nice.xsh; native test test_nice_failed_advisory_write_stops_the_command (skipped when /dev/full is missing or as root).

tests/timeout/timeout-parameters.sh.note: A negative value that underflows (' -1e-10000') is invalid, and zero is tested with inequalities because -0.0 != 0.0 in XSH. core/lib/proc_launch.xsh interval; native test timeout_underflowing_intervals_keep_their_sign.

tests/timeout/timeout.sh.note: The only failing step is (trap '' PIPE && timeout 10 yes |:) | grep 'Broken pipe'. The staged yes applet (core/yes.xsh, not owned) exits silently on EPIPE, while GNU prints 'yes: standard output: Broken pipe'. All other steps pass with the worktree timeout.
